transcript:
User: I want to be upfront: the last marketing agency strung me along for three months and I got nothing. Why would you be different?
Agent: Got it, that’s really frustrating — three months is a long time to feel like nothing’s happening.  

Quick thing so I don’t make the same mistakes they did: what exactly did they promise you that never showed up — more calls, booked jobs, certain ad results?
User: They promised more booked appointments and consistent communication, but once I signed, they disappeared.
Agent: Yeah, that makes total sense — if they went quiet after you signed, that’s a trust problem, not just a results problem.  

So I don’t assume: were they actually handling your phone calls too, or was it mostly ads/online leads and your team handled the phones?
User: They focused on ads and online leads. My team managed the calls; that's where the gaps were.
Agent: Gotcha, so they tried to fill the top of the funnel and the leaks were actually on the phones.  

When those new leads — or any customers — call and no one picks up, what usually happens next: do they leave a voicemail, call back later, or just move on to the next company?
User: Most just move on. We miss about 18 calls a week, and it really adds up.
Agent: Yeah, that absolutely adds up — 18 shots a week you’ll probably never see again.  

So instead of another agency “promising” more leads, what if we just made sure every one of those 18 callers was answered, qualified, and either booked or at least captured — is that the part you actually want fixed?
User: Exactly. I need assurance those missed calls are handled. What happens once I decide to work with you?
Agent: Makes total sense — you want to know what actually happens after you say yes, not more vague promises.  

So once you’re on board, we set up a system that answers every missed call right away, talks to the caller like a real receptionist, captures their info, and books appointments directly into your calendar instead of letting them walk — can I ask, are you mainly trying to plug those 18 missed calls a week, or are after-hours calls a problem too?
User: Mainly missed calls. After-hours aren't a big issue, but it’s the daytime ones that hurt us.
Agent: Got it, so it’s those daytime calls slipping through while everyone’s busy that are stinging.  

When a call comes in during the day and you miss it, is there anyone dedicated to the phones, or is it whoever’s free between jobs trying to grab it?
User: It's whoever's free, which isn't often enough. We're juggling patients and can't always be at the phone.
Agent: Totally hear you — if everyone’s with patients, the phone’s basically competing with your actual work.  

So I can be specific: in a typical week when you miss those 18 calls, are you more worried about losing brand-new patients, or existing patients trying to reschedule and getting frustrated?
User: I'm more worried about losing brand-new patients who might not call back if we miss them.
Agent: Yeah, that stings the most — brand‑new patients usually don’t give you a second chance.  

So I’m clear on the outcome you’re looking for: if our system could automatically grab those missed daytime calls, qualify the patient, and drop a booked slot straight into your schedule, what would you need to see in the first 30–60 days to feel “this is working and not like the last agency”?
User: I need to see real, booked appointments and consistent follow-up, not just empty promises.
Agent: Totally fair — you want proof in your calendar and in your inbox, not in a slide deck.  

So… how many extra new-patient appointments per week would feel like, “okay, this is clearly working” for you — 3–5, 8–10, or more?
User: I'd say 8–10 new patient appointments would be a clear indicator that it's working for us.
Agent: Gotcha, 8–10 new-patient bookings a week is your “this is real” number.  

And just so I’m lining things up right: are you mainly hoping to fix this because those missed calls are slowing growth, or because you personally don’t have the bandwidth to babysit another agency-style setup?
User: Both. I want growth without babysitting another agency. I need something that works without constant oversight.
Agent: Totally makes sense — you want growth that doesn’t depend on you hovering over another vendor.  

So I can connect the dots for you: you’re missing about 18 calls a week from brand‑new patients during the day; if we could automatically answer those, qualify them, and book 8–10 of them straight into your schedule without you lifting a finger, would you want to see what that setup looks like in a quick walkthrough with Jay, our founder?
User: Okay... one demo. But I'm watching closely. Let's schedule that walkthrough. My number's +16025550004.
Agent: Got it, you’re cautious and you should be — we’ll let the demo speak for itself.  

What’s usually better for you for a 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay, no commitment at all — earlier in the day or later in the afternoon?
User: Earlier in the day works best. Please remember, I'm in Mountain/Phoenix time. Looking forward to seeing how it works.
Agent: Got it, earlier in the day in Mountain/Phoenix time, and you’re watching this closely — totally fair.  

What does your morning usually allow for a 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay, no commitment — closer to 9–10, or more like 11?
User: Let's aim for closer to 10 AM Mountain/Phoenix time. I want to see how this could fit in.
Agent: Perfect, closer to 10 works well and we’ll keep everything in Mountain/Phoenix time.  

Which day is better for that 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay, no commitment — tomorrow morning or the following day?
User: Tomorrow morning at 10 AM Mountain/Phoenix time works for me. Looking forward to the demo with Jay.
Agent: Nice, that timing’s clear — tomorrow at 10 AM Mountain/Phoenix time with Jay for a 20‑minute, no‑commitment walkthrough to see how we can turn those missed calls into booked new‑patient appointments.  

Before we wrap, is there anything specific you want Jay to focus on in the demo — like how we book into your schedule, how the calls sound, or how we prove it’s actually working?
User: Focus on how you book into our schedule and prove it's working. I need to see results.
Agent: Gotcha, that helps a lot — we’ll keep it tight and focused on results.  

So tomorrow at 10 AM your time, Jay will: walk through exactly how we plug into your schedule to book new patients, and show how you’ll see proof it’s working (call logs, booked appointments, and outcomes), so you’re not guessing.  

One last thing so we’re prepared: what scheduling system are you using right now for patients (Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental, something else)?
User: We use Dentrix for our scheduling. Just ensure everything integrates smoothly without disrupting our current system.
Agent: Gotcha, Dentrix — that’s helpful, and we’ll keep everything wrapped around your current flow, not fighting it.  

Jay can walk you through exactly how we sync with Dentrix and show, on-screen, where you’ll see those booked new‑patient appointments and tracking — anything else you want him to be ready for before tomorrow at 10 your time?
User: That's it for now. Just ensure Jay's ready to show tangible results. Looking forward to it.
Agent: Sounds good — Jay will be ready to walk you through exactly how we plug into Dentrix, how bookings show up, and how you can clearly see the results, not just hear promises. If anything comes up before tomorrow at 10 your time, you can bring it to that call and we’ll tackle it live — talk to you then, and have a great rest of your day.

chat_analysis.chat_summary: The user, frustrated by a previous agency's lack of results and communication, discussed their need for a reliable solution to handle missed daytime calls and book new patient appointments. The agent addressed the user's concerns, clarified expectations, and scheduled a demo with the founder to showcase integration with Dentrix and proof of results. The user confirmed the demo time and specified their priorities for the walkthrough.
